text:
Ciara: hey team, seeing a weird perf regression on long-context flows — continuous-batcher is merging batches that straddle KV fragment boundaries and then we hit a head-of-line stall for ~30-80ms while the pager rehydrates pages. repro on staging with `--longctx=80k`
Ben: ugh. can you paste a tiny log snippet?
Ciara: yeah, here's the critical window:
```\n[2025-06-23T18:12:05Z] batch-merge id=0x7f frag_range=0x1000-0x2fff merged_with=0x3000-0x4fff\n[2025-06-23T18:12:05Z] kv-pager miss keys=120 rehydrate_ms=52\n[2025-06-23T18:12:05Z] batch-hol-block id=0x7f wait_for=kv-pager\n[2025-06-23T18:12:05Z] batch-resume id=0x7f latency_ms=78\n```\nAlice M.: interesting, so merge decision doesn't check "frag affinity" before combining. that would explain extra pager thrash. :thinking:
Mike: do we have telemetry that ties batch merge decisions to fragment hotness? iirc we only sample per-slot occupancy, not frag boundaries.
Ciara: correct — current heuristic: merge if (age>X && size<Y). no frag-awareness. profiler shows large tail in `kv_pager::rehydrate` correlating with merged batches that include >1 fragment.
Sara: could also be fragmentation growth over long contexts — repeated prefix caching leading to thinly filled fragments so merges happen frequently.
Ben: quick mitigation: disallow merging across fragment-aligned offsets. e.g., if end_of_batch % FRAG_SZ != 0 && start_of_next % FRAG_SZ != 0 then skip merge. cheap to check.
Mike: downside is smaller batches for those cases => higher p99 tokens. but might drop pager misses significantly. do we have an A/B test harness?
Ciara: yes, I ran a small A/B on staging: toggle `merge_across_frag=false` gave p99 token latency down 24% and pager rehydrates down 45% for longctx. throughput dropped ~3%.
perf-bot: [perf/regression] toggle/merge_across_frag=false: p50 +1.2%, p95 -18.3%, p99 -24.1%, pager_miss_rate -45%
Alice M.: that looks promising. longer-term: we should feed frag-boundary metrics into the batching score so we can prefer merges inside same-frag and only merge across frags if expected cost reduction > pager penalty.
Ciara: agreed. next steps: (1) ship the quick toggle to prod on a small fleet, (2) add frag-awareness metric to batch scoring, (3) add unit test that simulates fragment boundary merges to prevent regressions.
Ben: I'll draft the PR for the toggle + unit tests. @Mike can you prototype the scoring change?
Mike: yep will spike this afternoon.
Sara: also flagging for ops — if you enable toggle we should watch mem pressure and also the `kv_pager.rehydrate_ms` histogram.
Ciara: thanks all — attaching the lightweight repro script in thread files. will follow up with numbers after a prod canary. :thumbsup:
